Maya (support): Hey team, Acme reported that their VSCode extension streaming requests keep failing mid-response. They see 'broken pipe' on our gateway and are being billed as 5xx. Escalating.
Juan (eng): Can you paste the gateway logs + request id?
Maya (support): Request id req_0a1b2c3d, customer said it happens ~30% of streams, mostly when a user cancels inside VSCode. Log snippet:```[gateway] 2026-03-10T18:02:11Z req=req_0a1b2c3d upstream_error="write tcp ...: broken pipe" client=54.23.11.9```
AcmeApp (customer): repro steps: 1) open prompt in VSCode ext 2) hit generate 3) click stop while streaming. Often they get a 500 error in client and we see billing for full tokens.
Eli (ops): Hmm we have a heuristic that maps midstream connection reset -> 5xx if upstream returned an error code OR connection closed before first chunk. Might be misclassifying client-initiated aborts.
Juan (eng): Do we have HTTP-level traces? Need to know if we saw final chunk/trailer. Can you grab the full proxy trace for req_0a1b2c3d?
Maya (support): Paste from customer side too, they sent this curl reproducer:```curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d $PAYLOAD``` They say: if they ctrl-c quickly we still get a 500 back to the app.
Eli (ops): I pulled gateway trace:```proxy: read error: connection reset by peer; upstream response bytes=1450; status=200->closed``` That suggests upstream sent data but client closed socket mid-stream.
Juan (eng): If upstream produced bytes and then client closed, we shouldn't classify as server 5xx. Our billing pipeline looks at final HTTP status recorded by the gateway; if the connection died before 200 finalization we mark 5xx. Need to confirm code path.
Maya (support): Customer is asking for billing credit for those aborted streams — they say it's happening for many users in VSCode. They provided app logs with timestamps.
AcmeApp (customer): FYI we only cancel from client side, not sending any explicit abort. VSCode extension just drops connection.
Juan (eng): Action: I'll add a debug flag to the gateway to capture abort reason for a 24h period and a small metric to count "client-abort-after-data" separately. Also want to change classification rule: if upstream wrote >0 bytes and there is no upstream error, mark as client-abort (4xx-like) for billing.
Eli (ops): For short-term relief I'll add a rule in metering to exclude requests with header X-Client-Abort: true (we can inject via proxy) while we verify. Will coordinate a rollout at 22:00 PST to avoid spike.
Maya (support): Thanks. Can we also collect a small trace from the customer's VSCode -> they said it uses a proxy extension (corporate proxy) sometimes. Could be proxy sending FIN.
Juan (eng): Good call. If corporate proxy is doing half-close semantics we might see a FIN from client that gateway treats as error. Ask customer to reproduce with direct network if possible.
SupportBot: Incident created: INC-2026-1573 linked to thread req_0a1b2c3d — assigned to Juan, Eli.
Maya (support): I'll ask Acme to try direct network and capture tcpdump. Will update thread when they send pcap. :eyes:
Juan (eng): Plan: (1) collect traces 24h, (2) temp metering exclusion, (3) change classification logic, (4) postmortem + billing remediation if we confirm misbilling.
Eli (ops): I'll schedule the exclusion roll at 22:00 PST and add extra logs for the next 48h.
Maya (support): Great, looping in billing if we confirm, and will keep Acme updated. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
